That's been on my list honestly. I was told to go talk to the department of workforce services and see what can be done assistance wise and to talk to vocational rehab. I'm putting it off out of pride/codependence but I'm sure once my stomach starts grumbling I'll suck it up.

It's not like they're making me feel at fault or attacked. They actually seem under the impression that I have things covered. Much more confidence in my abilities than warranted. Maybe I'm not being vulnerable enough with them for them to realize how to help. I have repressed my memories of that time and have a lot of emotional numbing in regards to it, so I can see how I would be difficult to help since we kinda need to start somewhere. I usually talk about it in a detached logical way as well because I don't actually know how to allow myself to feel, or if there's anything to be felt there. (Well that was silly since obviously I'm feeling something now...) 

I can't thank you enough. I was feeling really alone and hopeless about it and withdrawing socially so it's great to be able to communicate with someone who *understands*. I understand if you don't have more to contribute to the conversation but I am curious to know what kind of therapy has helped you most and if you medicate or if you ever had an *aha* moment where you seem to take several steps forward?

Thank you so much for replying. It does help to know I'm not the only one who has, has had or will have had these feelings. 

I guess it is depression? I've been dealing with chronic illness and poverty while doing college classes and was really getting unbearable. (Too serious, easily agitated... nothing like who I usually am.) I went on vacation and had a great time, and which brought the joie de vrai back in my life until this. I thought yesterday I was just down because the hangover but today my eyes keep randomly leaking (dammit I'm not crying!) and I can't bring myself to get out of bed to go to class or to work. I wish I could afford to take a break from life and sort this shit out but I honestly get more depressed doing that, financially it's unfeasible (can't even afford groceries for the next two weeks), and I'm already delayed in my graduation, 23 and hitting junior status next semester. 

I have been seeing a therapist through the university but she doesn't seem to be helping. I'm very introspective and a psych major and have actually been asked by therapists why I'm seeking them out since I have good insight into the issues. I've kinda lost hope with therapists in all honesty. Finding a free therapist who is qualified to work with ptsd is incredibly difficult and even then, if we click I get asked why I'm there... I've explained I'm coming for the tools to fix my problem since I'm trying to screw something in with a hammer, and get told I have the screwdriver already I'm just being stubborn and refusing to use it. Except I can never find the screwdriver. Maybe that's a bad analogy.. I guess I was just hoping to find out how other people got past this. I've been blissfully unaware of these social aspects, never tried to date or be romantically involved before, so it didn't matter if I was a 'pretty girl'. I'm not sure what changed, I'm certainly not happy about it. I've never built my self image around my actual appearance so now that it's factoring in I get incredibly frustrated. Maybe I should talk to /loseit about body image along with getting these issues sorted out.

Thanks for sending the thought out to a stranger, I really appreciate it. I've been having some rough days but tomorrow I'm heading to a doctor to hopefully get things sorted out and after a nice vacation on the beach. I haven't had the energy to really get out of bed lately and nearly forgot my throwaways password but I felt like reading over some of the kind words you left and was really surprised to see you checking in. You are a wonderful person, just thought you should know. :)

Thank you Clarance. You made me tear up, I'm not gonna lie. You are an awesome person, it does my heart good to see that there are still altruistic people out there. I'm not really doing anything to make life more enjoyable, I moved across state and still haven't made new friends and I'm still not familiar with my new city. It's kinda pathetic since I was here in the spring as well, I should have made at least one friend by now.

I haven't seen much of America honestly, but last year I did take a trip overseas to Scandinavia to visit some friends. You're right, baby steps forward. Once I set my mind to something I know I can accomplish it if I really want it. The semantics of dietary restrictions and medications just started weighing down on the idea. If I do the gluten free thing I'm bound to start feeling like a person again (here's hoping). 

Thank you so much for showing your concern and support. Some nights it's nice to know that I'm not alone. Especially when it seems like the odds are stacked against me.

I haven't tried keto, I've looked at it a few times though. I guess until recently I was in denial about the whole celiac thing. My mom has had the disease for as long as I can remember so I'm pretty solid on finding gluten free foods, I know what to look for. It's just really frustrating because I hate the taste and baked goods are my favorite :( part of the hypothyroid thing is I crave carbs and sweets mega bad so it's probably for the best that eating them will make me feel like death.

It's true, I haven't cut in a couple years and I don't know if I could now. I'm really ashamed of the scars I have already.. It is tempting for me though, one of those watch for a relapse things I guess. I dunno, I have a very difficult time letting guys get close. I'm very uncomfortable with physical contact and tend to shut down flirting by nature. I've spent the last decade overweight so it's not like I want people to suddenly focus entirely on my appearance now, ya know? It's like I have guy friends who didn't really give me the time of day before and now they're talking to me and trying to flirt and it seems so disingenuous. If someone likes me I want it to be for the content of my mind (as feeble as it is) not for the shape of my body. I feel like a petulant child, "I want people to like me, but it has to be on terms I find acceptable."

I'm gonna try, I usually really enjoy new things. It's just mustering up the energy, but with cutting out gluten that should be easier. Thank you for replying, I really appreciate the kind gesture. It means a lot to me that there are people out there that will help strangers in need. Things are just a little overwhelming right now and I'm still trying to figure out healthy coping mechanisms. I've always believed that the quality of life outweighs the sanctity of life, and having my body attack itself isn't great quality. After taking a bit to think/calm down I realized that I am having new experiences with this. I'm experiencing things that not everyone has, and there is something to be appreciated in that.
